chunks: And with this chain of transmission, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from 'Ali ibn Abi al-Mughirah, from Maysarah, from Abi Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:
"Wudu (ablution) is one by one, one by one; and he described the ankle as being on the top of the foot."

key_terms.الْكَعْبَ: the ankle/bone referred to in the legal description of the foot
key_terms.الْوُضُوءُ: wudu (ablution), the ritual purification before acts of worship
key_terms.وَاحِدَةً: once; indicating a single performance of each act

ai.seo_question: How is wudu (ablution) performed in this hadith, and where is the ka'b located on the foot?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a brief legal description of wudu (ablution), indicating that its acts are to be performed once each. It also identifies the location of the ka'b in relation to the foot, which is relevant to the rules of ritual purification.
